newsitem.title: USA: Rivlin-U.S. economy performing very strongly--RFTV.
newsitem.headline: Rivlin-U.S. economy performing very strongly--RFTV.

text.p: Federal Reserve Board Vice Chairman Alice Rivlin on Thursday said the U.S. economy did not slow down in the first quarter as expected and was performing quite strongly.
Interviewed on Reuters Financial Television, Rivlin also said that labor markets remained tight and the risks were on the upside for an increase in inflation.

"Over the last few weeks, the signs have been quite uniform, this economy has been performing very strongly, which is basically good but it does raise the question of what would be happening a few months from now if it continues to grow so strongly," she said.
Asked if she thought the risks for inflation were increasing, Rivlin said that "I think almost anyone looking at this economy and trying to read the tea-leaves would say the risks are on the upside."
She added that "this economy is performing very strongly and when an economy is performing very strongly, the risks for overheating are there."
Rivlin also said that labor markets were very tight but she said there was something of a mystery why labor markets can be as tight as they are without wages and prices rising any faster.
"I don't think the Fed has all the answers, nor does anybody else, we're all feeling our way," she said.

Rivlin said productivity is rising faster than data accumulated by the government would suggest, which she said was one explanation of why tight labor markets have not generated an increase in prices.
She said the U.S. economy would benefit if economies overseas were stronger, adding that the outlook for the economies of America's trading partners seemed "at least moderately good."
Asked about the impact of the declining stock market, Rivlin said that it was uncertain whether this would lead to a reduction in consumer demand.
"Since we don't know what how much of the strong consumption has been attributable to the rise in the stock market, it's hard to predict how much a leveling out will affect it," she said.

Rivlin, in summing up, said on balance the economic news was mostly good, "but the job of the Fed is to think ahead, to think what can we do to sustain this good growth and tightness in the labor markets...which need to be sustained as long as they can."
